title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: The letter d is used both for the differential and for the number of closed new generators. This notational clash is in the original typescript.

Adjoining the killing generators ω_{d+1}..ω_r can create new kernel in H^{n+2}. In general (especially the non-simply-connected case) one must iterate, possibly infinitely often, within degree n+1 before injectivity in n+2 holds. The text's appeal to 'as in step 2' presumably covers this, but the single step as stated is incomplete.
'polynomical' is a typo in the original typescript.

ideas.what: Inductive construction of a minimal model Λ(V) → E, adding generators degree by degree to kill cohomology cokernel and kernel.
ideas.where_published: Sullivan, Publ. IHÉS 47 (1977); this page is a copy of Sullivan's text

ideas.what: Reading rational π_2, π_3, the Hurewicz map and the Whitehead product off the low-degree generators and the quadratic part of the differential.
ideas.modern_name: Dual of the quadratic differential = rational Whitehead product (homotopy Lie algebra)

missed.claim: Grothendieck placed Sullivan's minimal-model text beside his own computation of cosimplicial cochain objects over a general ring k as exterior/divided-power algebras on Ω_k. This suggests he was considering an integral, divided-power version of Sullivan's polynomial de Rham forms. The theme was later developed by others (Cenkl–Porter tame homotopy, divided-power forms, Mandell's E∞ integral models), without reference to this 1976 talk. Only a hint; the page itself contains no new mathematics.
missed.quote: Now suppose by induction that Λ(x_1, ..., x_n; y_1, y_2, ...; z_1, z_2, ...:d) →ρ_n E has been constructed
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck's unpublished 1976 IHÉS talk engaged with rational homotopy theory, an under-recorded early link between divided-power de Rham theory and integral models of homotopy types.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typed copy of Sullivan's standard minimal-model exposition, not Grothendieck's work. Its only interest is archival: it shows he read Sullivan while working on the divided-power de Rham complex.
transcription_corrections: Handwritten 'OS 5' in the top-right corner marks this as page 5 of an inserted typescript, apparently Sullivan's, not Grothendieck's handwriting.
'homotopy grou' is cut off at the page edge: read 'group'.
'poly-nomical' is spelled thus in the original typescript (for 'polynomial').
